Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Montfort Capital Corp. (TSXV: MONT) ("Montfort" or the "Company"), today announced financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026 and second quarter ended June 30, 2026. All figures are reported in Canadian dollars unless otherwise noted.

"The first and second quarter results continue to illustrate the trajectory of our financial performance, driven by growth in the loan portfolios of Langhaus and Nuvo and ongoing careful management of expenses," said Ken Thomson, CEO of Montfort. "We are now generating consistent positive cash flow from operations that is sufficient to support our substantially reduced overhead and reinvest in our lending portfolios. I would like to extend my sincere gratitude to our operating team, board of directors and financial partners whose effort and commitment has been fundamental to achieving these significantly improved results."

FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS

For the quarters ended March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026 the Company reports the following highlights:



To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/12878/324754_85a1c703f41149f1_001full.jpg

Three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended June 30, 2025:

  • Total revenue increased by $0.5 million or 75% compared to the prior year, primarily reflecting a $1.0 million increase in interest income on a larger loan portfolio, partially offset by a $0.6 million increase in interest and financing expenses.

  • Total expenses decreased by $0.2 million or 16% compared to the prior year, mainly due to lower administrative, management and directors' fees ($0.1 million) and amortization ($0.1 million), partially offset by a $0.1 million increase in accounting and legal fees.

  • Net and comprehensive income was $0.1 million, compared to net income of $5.6 million in the prior year, which included income from discontinued operations.

  • Net income from continuing operations was $0.1 million, compared to a net loss of $0.6 million in the prior year, an improvement of $0.7 million reflecting higher revenue and reduced operating expenses.

  • There were no discontinued operations in the current period. Income from discontinued operations of $6.1 million in the prior year included the gain on disposal of Brightpath of $8.7 million (sold April 2, 2025).

Six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the six months ended June 30, 2025:

  • Total revenue increased by $1.1 million or 101% compared to the prior year, primarily reflecting a $1.8 million increase in interest income from loan growth in Langhaus and Nuvo, partially offset by a $1.0 million increase in interest and financing expenses.

  • Total expenses decreased by $0.9 million or 32% compared to the prior year, primarily due to reductions in administrative, management and directors' fees ($0.3 million), amortization ($0.2 million), bad debts ($0.2 million) and share-based payments ($0.1 million).

  • Net and comprehensive income was $0.1 million, compared to net income of $0.6 million in the prior year, which included income from discontinued operations.

  • Net income from continuing operations was $0.1 million, compared to a net loss of $1.8 million in the prior year, an improvement of $1.8 million reflecting higher revenue and reduced operating expenses.

  • There were no discontinued operations in the current period. Income from discontinued operations of $2.4 million in the prior year included the gain on disposal of Brightpath of $8.7 million, partially offset by operating losses of Brightpath and Pivot, including expected credit losses of $5.7 million.

  • Loans receivable as at June 30, 2026, net of allowance, increased by $27.6 million or 13% compared to the balance at December 31, 2025, driven by loan growth in Langhaus ($18.2 million) and Nuvo ($9.4 million). Advances of $58.3 million were partially offset by settlements of $30.6 million.

This news release is qualified in its entirety by the Company's financial statements for the quarters ended March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026 and the associated Management's Discussion & Analysis, which can be downloaded from the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at https://www.sedarplus.ca/

About Montfort Capital Corp.

Montfort builds and manages private credit portfolios that have focused investing strategies for the institutional and accredited investors markets. For further information, please visit www.montfortcapital.com.

The Company originates, underwrites and manages secured loans through the following operating divisions:

Continuing Operations

Langhaus provides insurance policy-backed lending solutions to high-net-worth individuals and entrepreneurs in Canada. Langhaus' loans are collateralized by the assignment of the borrower's whole life insurance policy, personal and/or corporate guarantees and, in some cases, other tangible collateral.

Nuvo partners with Canadian alternative asset managers and ultra high-net-worth individuals to provide revolving net asset value based loans (ie. 'NAV loans').

Discontinued Operations

The Brightpath business was sold on April 2, 2025. Brightpath is a registered mortgage brokerage and mortgage administrator, administering a portfolio of mortgages secured by residential properties. As at December 31, 2024, the assets and liabilities of Brightpath were classified as held for sale and the operating results are included under discontinued operations up to the date of sale.

The Pivot business was sold on November 4, 2025. Pivot specializes in asset-based lending targeting SME borrowers in Canada. Sources of revenue include net interest income from loans receivable, origination fees and amendment fees. In addition, Pivot earns loan servicing fees and performance fee income for loan management services performed.

Payward has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire data-driven VC and asset manager Tribe Capital Management – making private markets the newest layer of Payward’s platform.

CHEYENNE, Wyo.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Payward, Inc., an integrated financial services and market infrastructure platform, today announced it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Tribe Capital Management, Inc., a venture capital and asset-management platform that uses AI and data science to underwrite and deploy capital across early- and late-stage private investments.

Customers increasingly demand access to early-stage companies, private-market opportunities, and emerging AI and technology investments. Tribe Capital’s capabilities across these segments will become a key part of Payward’s Asset Management pillar.

Tribe Capital brings investment sourcing, underwriting, portfolio construction, and fund-management capabilities that complement Payward’s existing infrastructure. They will expand the range of investment products available across Payward’s consumer, professional, and institutional client base.

“Joining Payward gives us the opportunity to bring Tribe’s investment approach to a global financial platform,” said Jonathan Hsu, co-founder of Tribe Capital. “We see a strong fit between our investment approach and Payward’s infrastructure, distribution, and product-building capabilities.”

Payward plans to build on Tribe Capital’s existing investment platform to develop new private-market offerings that draw on its infrastructure and distribution. The combination will connect investment origination and asset management with capabilities across custody, trading, collateral, and tokenization. Tribe Capital is expected to operate within Payward’s Asset Management pillar, alongside Trading, Banking, Services, and AI.

Tribe Capital, which has $2.7 billion in assets under management, invests across early- and late-stage private companies through commingled funds and co-investment vehicles. It was founded in 2018 on the premise that investment decisions in startups could be faster and better by paying close attention to operating and product-engagement data. Its portfolio spans companies applying AI and advanced software across technology and financial infrastructure.

The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including required consents, and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

Advisors

Moelis & Company LLC served as financial advisor to Payward, with Jones Day and Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz serving as legal counsel and Morrison Foerster serving as regulatory counsel. Ropes & Gray served as legal counsel to Tribe Capital.

About Payward

Payward, Inc. is an integrated financial services and market infrastructure platform advancing an open, global financial system. Built on a single shared architecture, Payward enables customers to hold, trade, earn, pay, and invest across asset classes without friction or fragmentation.

At its core, Payward provides the infrastructure layer behind Kraken and a growing set of purpose-built products, including NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, and CF Benchmarks.

Payward separates infrastructure from product expression. Each product surface is designed for a specific customer segment, regulatory regime, and use case, while operating on the same global foundation:

  • One global liquidity pool
  • One unified risk and margin engine
  • One collateral and settlement system
  • One compliance and licensing framework

This shared architecture allows Payward to scale efficiently, launch new products at low marginal cost, and serve diverse global markets while maintaining consistent risk management, regulatory integrity, and operational resilience.

About Tribe Capital Management

Tribe Capital is a venture capital firm focused on harnessing AI and data science to deploy capital with precision – into N-of-1 companies, including Shiprocket (NSE: SHIPROCKET), SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX), Applied Intuition, Apollo.io, and Kapital. Founded in 2018 by Arjun Sethi, Jonathan Hsu, and Ted Maidenberg. Headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with $2.7 billion in assets under management.

Key Terms

assets under managementfinancial
Assets under management (AUM) is the total value of all the investments that a financial company or fund is responsible for overseeing on behalf of its clients. It’s like a big bucket that shows how much money the firm is managing for people or organizations. A higher AUM often indicates a larger, more trusted company, and it can influence how much money they earn and the services they can offer.
commingled fundsfinancial
An investment vehicle that pools money from multiple investors into a single portfolio managed together; each investor owns a pro rata interest rather than specific, separately held securities. Commingled funds are often structured as trusts or partnership vehicles and are used by institutions and pooled accounts (for example retirement plan collective trusts), with the manager making buying and selling decisions for the combined pool; they can differ from mutual funds and ETFs in regulatory oversight, reporting, investor eligibility, and liquidity or redemption terms.
co-investment vehiclesfinancial
A co-investment vehicle is a fund-like arrangement that lets outside investors put money directly into a specific deal alongside a lead investor, rather than investing in the lead investor’s larger fund. Think of it like joining a neighbor to buy a single rental property instead of buying into their whole portfolio: it can cut fees and boost potential returns but concentrates risk and often has less liquidity, so investors need to weigh higher upside against greater exposure to one investment.

VALLEY FORGE, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) today reported financial results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 and provided guidance for fiscal year 2027.

HEADLINES

  • GAAP net income of $692 million and adjusted net income of $665 million compared to GAAP net income of $678 million and adjusted net income of $728 million in the prior year.
  • GAAP diluted earnings per share (“EPS”) of $3.12 and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.00 compared to GAAP diluted EPS of $3.09 and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.32 in the prior year.
  • Delivered adjusted diluted EPS that exceeded our revised guidance range issued on May 6, 2026, inclusive of approximately $0.10 cents of incremental tax benefits associated with the renewable natural gas facilities previously placed in service.
  • Achieved growth in reportable segments earnings before interest expense and income tax1 ("EBIT") of $1,198 million, when compared to $1,176 million in the prior year.
  • Strengthened the balance sheet with available liquidity of approximately $1.8 billion and a leverage ratio of 3.8x at UGI Corporation.
  • Invested approximately $900 million of capital, with 77% directed to our natural gas businesses, including completing the replacement of cast iron main at UGI Utilities nearly a year ahead of our February 2027 commitment.
  • Advanced portfolio optimization through divestiture of the LPG operations in seven countries and the pending sale of the PA Electric Utility for approximately $470 million, subject to customary closing conditions.
  • Subsequent to year-end, successfully concluded the gas base rate case at:
    • UGI Utilities, which comprised a two-phase, $65 million distribution rate increase ($40 million effective October 2026; $25 million effective October 2027) with a stay-out provision until January 2029.
    • Mountaineer Gas, a net revenue increase of $17 million effective December 1, 2026, with a stay-out provision until February 2028.
  • Issues Fiscal 2027 adjusted diluted EPS guidance range of $2.90 - $3.202.

“Fiscal 2026 was a year of disciplined execution and meaningful progress in reshaping UGI," said Robert Flexon, President and Chief Executive Officer of UGI Corporation. "We delivered year-over-year growth in EBIT, simplified our portfolio and strengthened our balance sheet, all while continuing to invest in the safety and reliability of the systems our customers depend on. At AmeriGas, the hard work of transforming the business continues with the team now increasing their focus on profitable volumetric growth. We enter the heating season well prepared to deliver safe, reliable service to our customers. Above all, we remain focused on creating long-term value for our shareholders, and today's announcement is the next step in that commitment."

2027 OUTLOOK
UGI provides an adjusted EPS guidance range of $2.90 - $3.202 per diluted share for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027. This guidance range assumes normal weather and the current tax regime.

EARNINGS CALL and WEBCAST
UGI Corporation will hold a live Internet Audio Webcast of its conference call to discuss Fiscal 2026 earnings and other current activities at 8:00 AM ET on Thursday, November 19, 2026. Interested parties may listen to the audio webcast both live and in replay on the Internet at https://www.ugicorp.com/investors/financial-reports/presentations or by visiting the company website https://www.ugicorp.com and clicking on Investors and then Presentations. A replay of the webcast will be available after the event through to 11:59 PM ET November 18, 2027.

ABOUT UGI
UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) is a distributor and marketer of energy products and services in the US and Europe. UGI offers safe, reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy solutions to customers through its subsidiaries, which provide natural gas transmission and distribution, electric generation and distribution, midstream services, propane distribution, renewable natural gas generation, distribution and marketing, and energy marketing services.

Comprehensive information about UGI Corporation is available on the Internet at https://www.ugicorp.com.

USE OF NON-GAAP MEASURES
Management uses “adjusted net income attributable to UGI Corporation” and "adjusted diluted earnings per share," both of which are non-GAAP financial measures, when evaluating UGI's overall performance. Management believes that these non-GAAP measures provide meaningful information to investors about UGI’s performance because they eliminate the impacts of (1) gains and losses on commodity and certain foreign currency derivative instruments not associated with current-period transactions and (2) other significant discrete items that can affect the comparison of period-over-period results. Volatility in net income attributable to UGI can occur as a result of gains and losses on commodity and certain foreign currency derivative instruments not associated with current-period transactions but included in earnings in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP").

Non-GAAP financial measures are not in accordance with, or an alternative to, GAAP and should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for, the comparable GAAP measures.

Updated data from a more mature October 2026 data cutoff show rapid and deep responses, with a 39% confirmed ORR, median duration of response of 9.2 months and median PFS of 6.7 months

Clinical activity consistent across HPV status and prior-treatment subgroups, with a manageable safety profile

Results support advancement of MICVO into the global Phase 3 HeadlinerSM trial in 2L+ R/M HNSCC, planned to initiate in mid-2027

Company to host a live webcast on November 19, 2026, at 7:00 a.m. EST, following the late-breaking oral presentation

BOSTON, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Pyxis Oncology, Inc. (Nasdaq: PYXS), a clinical-stage company developing next-generation therapeutics for difficult-to-treat cancers, today announced updated results from its ongoing global Phase 1 monotherapy study evaluating micvotabart pelidotin (MICVO) in patients with second-line and beyond recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (2L+ R/M HNSCC).

The results will be presented on November 19, 2026, by Faye Johnson, M.D., Ph.D., professor of thoracic/head and neck medical oncology at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, in a late-breaking oral presentation at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics in Barcelona, Spain.

The updated data, as of October 14, 2026, demonstrated a 39% confirmed objective response rate (cORR), 94% disease control rate (DCR), median progression-free survival (mPFS) of 6.7 months, 12-month overall survival (OS) probability of 81%, and newly reported median duration of response (mDOR) of 9.2 months among 33 efficacy evaluable patients dosed at 5.4 mg/kg intravenously once every three weeks with a dose equivalent to or below a dose cap. Together, these results provide further evidence of clinical activity across HPV statuses and prior-treatment subgroups, with an expected and manageable tolerability profile.

“We are grateful to the EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium for highlighting these updated MICVO data in 2L+ R/M HNSCC, and to Dr. Johnson for presenting these important new results,” said Tom Civik, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Pyxis Oncology. “The data from October show improvements across multiple key clinical activity endpoints with a novel analysis showing that MICVO increased mPFS by 50% versus the most recent prior therapy patients had received before MICVO. We are also very happy to report that our clinical strategy for managing safety has had the intended impact. There have been no new cases of Grade 3 peripheral neuropathy and the six patients that experienced Grade 3 peripheral neuropathy have all improved with five of the six patients resolving to Grade 1 or better. Collectively, this updated data profile, and the new analyses further support our plan to advance MICVO into the global Phase 3 HeadlinerSM trial in 2L+ R/M HNSCC, which we expect to initiate in mid-2027. With important regulatory meetings in the near term and more mature overall survival (OS) data expected in the first half of 2027, we remain confident in our path forward.”

“For patients whose disease progresses after platinum chemotherapy and immunotherapy, there remains a substantial unmet medical need, particularly as we anticipate broader use of EGFR-targeted therapies in earlier lines of treatment,” said Dr. Johnson. “It is reassuring to see responses that last in this setting and, if confirmed in a larger study, MICVO could potentially offer these patients a meaningful new treatment option.”

To participate in the live webcast, participants may register in advance here. The event and accompanying slides can be accessed by visiting the investor relations section of the Company's website at https://ir.pyxisoncology.com. An archived webcast will be available on the Company's website following the event.

About Micvotabart Pelidotin (MICVO)
Micvotabart pelidotin (MICVO, formerly PYX-201) is an investigational antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) that uniquely targets extradomain-B of fibronectin (EDB+FN), a non-cellular structural component of the tumor extracellular matrix. MICVO is designed to generate a multi-pronged attack on difficult-to-treat cancers by directly killing cancer cells, reducing extracellular matrix density, inhibiting tumor angiogenesis and mobilizing an anti-tumor immune response.

MICVO received Fast Track Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for the treatment of adult patients with R/M HNSCC whose disease has progressed following treatment with platinum-based chemotherapy and an anti-PD-(L)1 therapy.

About Pyxis Oncology
Pyxis Oncology, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing therapeutics for difficult-to-treat cancers. The Company’s lead candidate, micvotabart pelidotin (MICVO), is a first-in-concept antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) that targets extradomain-B of fibronectin (EDB+FN), a non-cellular structural component of the tumor extracellular matrix (ECM). EDB+FN is selectively overexpressed in the tumor microenvironment of a wide range of solid tumors and largely absent from normal adult tissues. MICVO is designed to treat solid tumors through a three-pronged mechanism of action: direct cancer cell killing, bystander effect and immunogenic cell death. MICVO is currently being evaluated as monotherapy in a Phase 1 clinical study in patients with recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (R/M HNSCC) and in combination with Merck’s anti-PD-1 therapy, KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) in a Phase 1/2 clinical study in patients with R/M HNSCC and other solid tumors. Pyxis Oncology is focused on advancing MICVO, with the goal of improving outcomes for patients living with R/M HNSCC and contributing to meaningful progress in cancer treatment.

To learn more, visit www.pyxisoncology.com or follow us on LinkedIn.

Planned Separation Intended to Unlock Long-Term Shareholder Value and Create Two Companies, Each a Leader in Its Respective Industry With Tailored Capital Allocation Priorities, Attractive Dividend Yield, and Meaningful Growth Opportunities

Enhances Strategic and Financial Flexibility for Each Company

Establishes UGI Corporation as a Premier Natural Gas Infrastructure Company Operating in Favorable U.S. Load-Growth Markets and Low-Cost Supply Regions

New Global LPG Company Expected To Be The Largest Publicly Listed LPG Distribution Company in The World Following The Separation

UGI Corporation to Host Conference Call and Webcast on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 8:00 AM ET

VALLEY FORGE, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--UGI Corporation (NYSE: UGI) today announced that its Board of Directors unanimously approved a plan to pursue the separation of its Global LPG business (the new LPG Company) from UGI to create two publicly traded companies, each well-capitalized with tailored capital allocation strategies and strongly positioned to serve customers, pursue strategic growth objectives and create significant, long-term shareholder value. UGI intends to execute the separation through a spinoff of the new LPG Company that is expected to be tax-free to UGI and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The spinoff is expected to be completed during the second half of calendar year 2027.

“The creation of the new LPG Company is the next step in our company’s transformation, building on the portfolio optimization, balance sheet strengthening, and operational improvements we have achieved. The separation positions both companies for long-term growth, strategic optionality, and significant value creation for shareholders and customers,” said President and Chief Executive Officer, Robert Flexon. “Each company will have distinct strategies and operating priorities with capital allocation and supporting resources directed to its greatest opportunities for success and market leadership.”

Flexon continued, “We move forward with great confidence in the future of both companies and their respective abilities to serve customers and communities with excellence.”

Anticipated Benefits of the Planned Separation

As separate companies, the New UGI and the new LPG Company are expected to benefit from:

  • Sharper strategic alignment: Focused management and business models aligned with each company’s markets, customers, and capital needs;
  • Tailored capital structures: Balance sheets and capital return policies aligned to each company’s financial profile and cost of capital;
  • Capital and strategic flexibility: Investments aligned with each company’s growth opportunities and other long-term shareholder value-creating alternatives; and
  • Distinct investment profiles: Discrete business models allowing investors to assess each company based on its operational and financial characteristics.

New UGI: A Premier Natural Gas Infrastructure Company in the Mid-Atlantic Region

Following the completion of the separation, the New UGI will be a premier natural gas infrastructure company with fully regulated natural gas utilities and complementary midstream assets located in a favorable long-term supply basin, with direct access to low-cost Marcellus and Utica supply, and ideally positioned to serve customers demanding safe, reliable, and affordable natural gas in the Mid-Atlantic region. Demand megatrends for natural gas, including the need for generation to support the power grid, data center development, and rising industrial activity, are expected to further drive sustainable growth for the New UGI. Its operations will include:

  • UGI Utilities, Inc.: Operates the second largest regulated natural gas utility in Pennsylvania, serving approximately 700,000 customers across 46 counties;
  • Mountaineer Gas Company: The largest regulated natural gas utility in West Virginia, serving more than 209,000 customers across 55 counties; and
  • UGI Energy Services, LLC: Includes natural gas pipeline and gathering assets with a total capacity of 5.1 MMDth/day and storage facilities with approximately 15 Bcf of capacity, as well as LNG peaking assets.

The New UGI is expected to benefit from consistent earnings growth and solid, recurring cash flows backed by a constructive regulatory framework that allows over 90% recoverability of capital spend within 12 months, a $5 billion regulated rate base expected to grow 8 – 10% per year, and fee-based contract structures covering more than 80% of midstream margins. Approximately 90% of the New UGI’s margins are de-risked through its regulated utility operations, take-or-pay and minimum volume commitments, and fixed-fee arrangements. Cash flows for the New UGI are expected to be directed to capital investments that promote safe, reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy; targeted system expansion opportunities; maintaining a strong balance sheet and investment-grade credit profile; and an attractive dividend for shareholders.

As a regulated utility and in keeping with UGI’s current focus on affordability and service excellence, the separation transaction should not have an impact on customers or customer rates.

New LPG Company: The Largest Publicly Traded LPG Distribution Company in the World Following the Separation

The new standalone LPG Company is expected to be a scaled leader in Europe and the largest retail propane distributor in the United States. The new LPG Company’s assets meet critical energy needs in the regions it serves and are strategically located near diverse supply channels, providing a competitive advantage that has resulted in a broad and diverse customer base spanning the residential, commercial, industrial, and agricultural sectors. With resilient unit margins, a targeted EBITDA margin of 17 – 20%, and expected growth in free cash flow, the new LPG Company will be well positioned to deliver a compelling and growing dividend, combined with share repurchases, while investing in targeted growth opportunities. Its operations will include:

  • UGI International: A leading distributor of LPG in nine countries in western and northern Europe and the largest in France, Belgium, Denmark, Luxembourg and Finland; and
  • AmeriGas Propane, Inc.: Serves approximately 950,000 customers in 49 states from approximately 1,300 distribution locations and a network of more than 41,700 cylinder-exchange outlets.

Contract structures and hedging programs within the new LPG Company will continue to support strong cash flow generation. UGI International has a track record of solid operational execution, and AmeriGas Propane has made meaningful progress on its operating improvement and safety initiatives while strengthening its balance sheet, leaving the business better positioned for volumetric growth. Building on these efforts will be a priority for the new LPG Company as it enters its next phase of growth.

Following the separation, cash flows for the new LPG Company, are expected to be directed to a compelling and growing dividend, share repurchases, and targeted strategic growth investments, while maintaining a strong balance sheet and industry-leading credit profile.

Key Terms

spinofffinancial
A spinoff is when a company separates part of its business into a new, independent company and gives existing shareholders shares in that new business. For investors, it matters because the move can clarify what each business is worth, let the separate companies focus on their own goals, and change risk and return — similar to converting one mixed-use property into two specialized apartments that may attract different buyers and rents.
ebitda marginfinancial
EBITDA margin is the share of each dollar of sales that a company keeps as operating cash profit before interest, taxes, and accounting for equipment wear and long-term investments. Think of it like the cash a store has left from every sale after paying day-to-day running costs but before paying rent, loan interest or replacing old machinery. Investors use it to compare core profitability and operational efficiency across companies by removing financing and accounting differences.
non-gaapfinancial
Non-GAAP refers to financial measures that companies use to show their earnings or performance without including certain expenses or income that are often added back to give a different picture. It matters because it can make a company's results look better or more favorable, but it may also hide important costs, so investors need to look at both GAAP (official rules) and non-GAAP numbers to get a full understanding.

form 10regulatory
Form 10 is a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission filing companies use to register their securities and become subject to public reporting requirements, delivering a comprehensive package of business descriptions, audited financial statements, management information and risk factors. For investors it matters because it creates a standardized, permanent dossier on a company—like a full inspection and disclosure packet when buying a house—so you can assess finances, risks and management and compare firms reliably.

Two leading global institutional investors, including a top-five asset manager by assets under management, make PIPE raise commitments. Committed PIPE now totals $17.1 million ahead of the proposed Nasdaq listing

DUNCAN, Okla., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- REEcycle Holdings, Inc. (“REEcycle”), a U.S.-based rare earth recycling company, and Hall Chadwick Acquisition Corp. (Nasdaq: HCAC, HCACU, HCACR) (“HCAC”) today announced that they have secured an additional $15.0 million in Private Investment in Public Equity (“PIPE”) commitments from two global asset managers that are existing REEcycle shareholders, in connection with their proposed business combination (the “business combination”) and Nasdaq listing.

Both institutional investors previously invested in REEcycle, and the new $15.0 million commitments will bring their total combined investment in REEcycle to $25.2 million. Together with the $2.1 million previously committed by entities affiliated with REEcycle’s Executive Chairman and HCAC’s sponsor, total PIPE commitments raised in connection with the business combination now equal $17.1 million.

All PIPE commitments, including those of the insiders, are at $10.00 per share. However, the two institutional investors will also receive an aggregate of 999,999 HCAC shares as an additional equity incentive at closing for no additional consideration. These incentive shares will be sourced from shares issuable to certain advisors to HCAC and REEcycle, including the Advisor Shares issuable to HC Singapore and REEcycle as consideration in the business combination and accordingly, will not increase the total number of HCAC shares to be issued in connection with the business combination.

In accordance with the terms of the definitive PIPE agreements, the PIPE commitments will fund immediately prior to closing of the business combination. Closing of the business combination is conditioned on a minimum aggregate cash amount at closing of $40.0 million, and the other conditions described in the registration statement on form S-4 filed by HCAC and REEcycle with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in connection with the business combination (the “Registration Statement”), which was declared effective on November 12, 2026.

Strategic Context

REEcycle is U.S.-based technology company focused on the recovery of rare earth elements from end-of-life magnets. REEcycle uses patented systems and processes for the extraction and recovery of rare earth elements from permanent magnets to produce a mixed rare earth oxide (MREO) for use by downstream processors in the manufacture of new permanent magnets and other industrial applications. These permanent magnets are used in a range of applications, including defense applications, hard disk drives (HDDs) found in desktop computers, laptops, and large server storage systems such as data centers, electric vehicle drive motors and regenerative braking systems, wind turbine generators, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) machines, power tools, and other advanced technologies. 

According to the Center for Strategic & International Studies, China controls approximately 90% of global rare earth processing capacity and exercises near-monopoly control over the processing of heavy rare earth elements such as dysprosium and terbium. The concentration of rare earth mining, separation and magnet manufacturing outside the U.S., together with the export controls and licensing requirements imposed by China on certain REEs and magnets beginning in April 2025 and escalating in July 2026, has increased the strategic focus of the U.S. government and commercial end-users on establishing secure domestic supply. REEcycle’s proprietary process recovers critical rare earth elements as part of its standard MREO output, making it a structurally important domestic sourcing alternative.

REEcycle’s operations in Duncan, Oklahoma, are supported by a previously announced $5.1 million Defense Production Act Title III award to advance domestic critical minerals supply.

Proceeds from the financing and closing of the business combination are intended to advance REEcycle from its current demonstration operations in Duncan to commercial-scale production.

Management Commentary

Mick McMullen, Executive Chairman of REEcycle, commented:

“Two investors who know our business well have chosen to increase their stake. This capital will help us move from demonstration to commercial scale, and recycling end-of-life magnets is the fastest route to domestic supply of the magnet rare earths that U.S. defense and industry rely on.”

Justin Froneman, Chief Executive Officer of REEcycle, commented:

“With this funding committed, our priority is execution. We are focused on ramping operations at our large-scale demonstration facility in Duncan, feedstock supply agreements and first offtake.”

Alex Bono Chief Executive Officer of Hall Chadwick Acquisition Corp, commented:

“This financing strengthens REEcycle’s position heading into closing and moves the transaction meaningfully toward meeting the minimum cash condition. Our focus now is completing the business combination for HCAC shareholders.”

The PIPE shares have not been registered under the Securities Act. The form of subscription agreement will be filed by HCAC with the SEC on a Current Report on Form 8-K.

About the Proposed Business Combination

REEcycle and HCAC entered into a business combination agreement dated May 31, 2026, valuing REEcycle at $400 million of total equity consideration, of which up to $50 million is contingent consideration payable only if REEcycle achieves a commercial production milestone.

The transaction is subject to a $40 million minimum cash condition, shareholder approval and other customary closing conditions.

Upon closing, the combined company is expected to be named REEcycle, Inc. and trade on Nasdaq under the proposed ticker symbol “REC”, subject to approval.

About REEcycle

REEcycle recovers rare earth elements from end-of-life permanent magnets using patented hydrometallurgical technology licensed from the University of Houston. Headquartered in Duncan, Oklahoma, the company is developing domestic rare earth recycling and processing capacity.

About Hall Chadwick Acquisition Corp.

HCAC is a Nasdaq-listed special purpose acquisition company focused on critical materials, infrastructure and energy, and defense-aligned technology. Its sponsor is Hall Chadwick Capital LLC.

FREMONT, Calif., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Enovix Corporation (“Enovix” or the “Company,” Nasdaq: ENVX), a developer and manufacturer of advanced lithium-ion batteries, today announced that it will distribute warrants to purchase Enovix common stock (“Warrants”) to its stockholders and certain convertible noteholders on November 18, 2026 (the “Distribution Date”), in accordance with the previously declared stockholder warrant dividend. As previously announced, each stockholder of record as of the close of business on November 13, 2026 (the “Record Date”) will receive one (1) Warrant for every four (4) shares of Enovix common stock held, rounded down to the nearest whole Warrant.

“Our first warrant dividend in 2025 demonstrated the strong support of our stockholders and their interest in participating directly in Enovix’s growth,” said Ryan Benton, Interim Chief Executive Officer. “This distribution builds on that by giving investors another way to participate while helping us address our outstanding debt by permitting Warrant exercises with the delivery of our 3.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2028 (the “2028 Notes”). Accepting our 2028 Notes at face value as payment of the exercise price allows us to retire debt and preserve cash for the business, while cash exercises provide additional funding that we could also apply toward retiring outstanding 2028 Notes and preserving flexibility to support execution on our priorities.”

Warrant Terms

Eligibility: Stockholders must have purchased or held shares no later than November 12, 2026 to be a stockholder of record as of the close of business on the November 13, 2026 Record Date and to receive Warrants.

Convertible Noteholders: Holders of our 2028 Notes and our 4.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2030 (the “2030 Notes”) as of the Record Date will also receive Warrants on a pass-through basis, as provided under the applicable indentures, at the same one-for-four ratio.

Receipt of Warrants: Eligible recipients do not need to take any action or make any payment to receive their Warrants. Holders may exercise, hold or sell the Warrants. Holders whose securities are held through an intermediary should contact that intermediary with questions about when the Warrants will appear in their accounts.

Cash Exercise Price: Each Warrant entitles the holder to purchase one (1) share of Enovix common stock for $3.00 in cash, subject to adjustments and amendments under the warrant agreement.

Note Exercise Alternative: In lieu of cash, holders may exercise 333 Warrants by delivering $1,000 principal amount of 2028 Notes. Unless otherwise permitted by Enovix, the 2030 Notes may not be used to exercise the Warrants.

Listing: The Warrants are expected to begin trading separately from Enovix common stock on Nasdaq under the symbol ENVXW on November 19, 2026, subject to applicable approvals.

Scheduled Expiration: April 28, 2028, at 5:00 p.m. New York City time, subject to early expiration and any extension under the warrant agreement.

Early Expiration Price Condition: This condition will be satisfied if the daily volume-weighted average price (“VWAP”) of Enovix common stock equals or exceeds 110% of the then-applicable exercise price, initially $3.30, on twenty (20) trading days within any thirty (30) consecutive trading-day period following issuance (the “Early Expiration Price Condition”). The qualifying trading days need not be consecutive.

If the Early Expiration Price Condition is satisfied, the Warrants will expire at 5:00 p.m. New York City time on the business day immediately following the final qualifying trading day, or a later date selected by the Company in accordance with the warrant agreement. Enovix will announce the applicable expiration date by press release.

Exercise Using Cash or 2028 Notes

Beginning on the Distribution Date, holders may exercise their Warrants using cash or 2028 Notes, subject to the warrant agreement.

The 2028 Notes are designated as eligible for exercise. The 2030 Notes are not eligible and may not be delivered as payment. The Company may, in its discretion and subject to the notice requirements and other terms of the warrant agreement, change the debt securities designated as eligible for exercise.

For cash exercises, each Warrant entitles the holder to purchase one (1) share of Enovix common stock for $3.00. For exercises using 2028 Notes, holders may deliver $1,000 principal amount of 2028 Notes for every 333 Warrants exercised and receive 333 shares. Note exercises must be submitted in whole multiples of this ratio, regardless of the market price of the 2028 Notes.

For example, a holder delivering $20,000 principal amount of 2028 Notes may exercise 6,660 Warrants and receive 6,660 shares of common stock.

The ability to exercise Warrants with 2028 Notes is available to any investor holding 333 Warrants for each $1,000 principal amount of 2028 Notes delivered. Warrants may be acquired through the dividend distribution or in the open market. Any investor may purchase additional Warrants in the market for exercise, and certain qualifying investors may purchase additional 2028 Notes in market transactions.

Any 2028 Notes delivered and accepted for exercise of Warrants will be cancelled, reducing Enovix’s outstanding debt and associated future interest obligations without requiring the Company to use cash to repay that principal. Enovix will receive cash proceeds only from cash exercises of the Warrants. Any cash proceeds will be available for general corporate purposes, including retiring 2028 Notes.

Exercise Procedures and Investor Resources

Holders whose Warrants or 2028 Notes are held through a broker, bank or other intermediary should contact that intermediary regarding receipt of their Warrants, exercise instructions, permitted payment methods and applicable deadlines.

The early expiration feature could substantially shorten the exercise period. Holders should make arrangements with their intermediaries in advance, as intermediaries may impose deadlines earlier than the Company’s deadline. Warrants not exercised before the applicable expiration deadline will expire without value.

The warrant agreement, prospectus supplement and related investor materials describe the complete terms, including exercise procedures, adjustments to the Warrants, any exercise suspension provisions and the conditions governing early expiration. Its proprietary silicon-anode battery architecture enables higher energy density and performance in space-constrained devices while maintaining safety and reliability, supporting commercialization across consumer and industrial markets.

MECHANICSBURG, Pa., Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pennsylvania American Water today completed its acquisition of the Indian Creek Valley Water Authority (ICVWA) water system for $32.8 million. The newly acquired system serves approximately 2,600 water customer connections in Ohiopyle Borough and portions of Bullskin, Connellsville, Saltlick, Springfield and Stewart townships in Fayette County and Donegal Borough and portions of Donegal and Mount Pleasant townships in Westmoreland County.

The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission (PUC) approved the acquisition on Sept. 10, 2026. Pennsylvania American Water will adopt the rates currently charged to the system's customers. ICVWA's decision in May 2025 to sell its water system to Pennsylvania American Water was made with customers in mind. With the acquisition, Pennsylvania American Water also welcomed four ICVWA employees to its local team and plans to hire two additional employees.

"We, as an Authority Board, are concerned about the long-term viability of serving water in our community," said Dave Cramer, Indian Creek Valley Water Authority board chairman. "We face many challenges and have limitations in our ability to invest in the system and maintain a large, spread-out network sourcing water from multiple locations. It has also become harder to meet Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection compliance. Partnering with Pennsylvania American Water makes sense due to their local engineering expertise and financial capacity to improve our system significantly."

Pennsylvania American Water is committed to investing approximately $9 million in improvements to the ICVWA system over the next five years of ownership to improve the quality and reliability of service. The company has a long and successful track record of providing solutions throughout the Commonwealth for water and wastewater systems facing significant capital investment needs and making the necessary and continued investments to meet current and future regulatory requirements. Learn more at pennsylvaniaamwater.com/infrastructure.

Pennsylvania American Water is pleased to welcome these residents spanning nine municipalities and two counties as our newest water customers," said Pennsylvania American Water President Justin Ladner. "We look forward to providing them with safe, clean, reliable and affordable water service by delivering on our technical expertise and extensive experience."

Customers will not see a rate increase when Pennsylvania American Water takes ownership of the system. The company will adopt the current rates. As the PUC regulates the company's rates and service rules, any future changes to rates must be reviewed and approved by the PUC.

Customers will be able to take advantage of the company's customer service benefits, including its online account management portal, MyWater, multiple options for bill payment and the company's longstanding H2O Help to Others Program™, which provides income-eligible customers with grants of up to $500 per year, significant discounts on monthly bills, debt forgiveness and water-saving devices and education.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported a net loss of $721,604, compared with a net loss of $76,175 in the corresponding period of 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported a net loss of $2,612,848, compared with a net loss of $1,841,317 in the corresponding period of 2025.

The reported comparative results for 2025 include the benefit of a non-recurring provision reversal of $1,041,431. During the third quarter of 2025, following the settlement of a claim, the Company reversed a previously recorded provision. This non-recurring, non-cash accounting adjustment favourably impacted the Company's reported net loss for both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

To provide additional context regarding year-over-year performance, excluding the benefit of this provision reversal, the comparative net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2025, would have been $1,117,606. Compared with this adjusted amount, the Company's net loss of $721,604 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, represents an improvement of $396,002.

Similarly, excluding the benefit of the provision reversal, the comparative net loss for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, would have been $2,882,748. Compared with this adjusted amount, the Company's net loss of $2,612,848 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, represents an improvement of $269,900.

These adjusted net loss comparisons are non-IFRS financial measures provided to assist investors in assessing the Company's year-over-year financial performance by excluding the impact of the non-recurring provision reversal recognized in the comparative period. These measures should be considered supplemental to, and not as a substitute for, net loss reported in accordance with IFRS.

Operational Revenue — Non-IFRS Financial Measure
Operational revenue is a non-IFRS financial measure that represents total billings under customer contracts, including monthly monitoring subscriptions, equipment rentals and sales, project management services, and installation activities. Operational revenue is not a standardized financial measure under IFRS and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies.

Operational revenue differs from reported IFRS revenue primarily because customer billings and revenue recognition under IFRS may occur in different periods depending on the nature of the customer arrangement and the applicable revenue recognition requirements. Accordingly, operational revenue should be considered as a supplemental measure of customer billings and not as a substitute for IFRS revenue.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, operational revenue totalled $2,017,811, compared with $2,188,275 in the corresponding period of 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, operational revenue increased to $7,685,237 from $6,551,066 in the corresponding 2025 period, representing an increase of $1,134,171, or approximately 17.3%.

Recurring Billings and Average Monthly Recurring Revenue — Non-IFRS Financial Measures
Recurring billings are a non-IFRS financial measure representing billings associated with the Company's contracted monthly monitoring and equipment arrangements. The measure is intended to provide supplemental information regarding the recurring billing component of the Company's business. Recurring billings are not equivalent to IFRS revenue and are not a standardized financial measure under IFRS.

The Company generates billings under a combination of monthly and annual customer arrangements. As a result, the timing of billings may differ from the timing of revenue recognition under IFRS. Management uses recurring billings and average monthly recurring revenue as supplemental operating measures when evaluating the Company's recurring billing activity.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, recurring billings totalled $969,805, compared with $790,452 in the corresponding period of 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, recurring billings increased to $2,966,321 from $2,518,251 in the corresponding 2025 period, representing an increase of approximately 17.8%.

Operating Metrics and Supplemental Business Indicators
The Company monitors certain operating metrics and supplemental business indicators that management uses to assess the deployment of its solutions, business development, customer demand and visibility into future contracted revenue. These metrics are not financial measures calculated in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards and should not be considered substitutes for IFRS financial measures or viewed in isolation as indicators of the Company's financial performance.

In-Building Devices
The Company monitors the number of in-building devices installed as an operating metric reflecting the deployment of its smart water metering and leak protection solutions.

As of September 30, 2026, Eddy had 145,847 in-building devices installed, compared with 125,832 as of September 30, 2025, representing year-over-year growth of approximately 16%.

The installed-device count is an operating metric used by management to monitor the deployment and adoption of the Company's solutions. While this metric provides an indication of the scale of the Company's installed device base, it does not, on its own, provide an indication of market share, customer retention, profitability or future financial performance.

Contracted Sales Backlog
The Company's contracted sales backlog is a supplemental operating metric used by management to assess market traction and demand for its leak-protection solutions and to monitor the estimated value of future contracted revenue. Given the nature of the new construction development cycle, revenue from contracts secured in a particular quarter generally materializes once construction commences, which typically occurs within several quarters to approximately two years following contract execution.

As at September 30, 2026, the Company's contracted sales backlog totalled approximately $39.65 million, compared with $35.43 million as at December 31, 2025, representing an increase of approximately $4.22 million, or 11.9%, during the nine-month period. The backlog represents the estimated value of future revenue associated with underlying customer agreements, which have a weighted average remaining term of approximately seven years. Accordingly, the backlog provides an indication of potential future revenue streams and reflects the long-term nature of the Company's customer relationships.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, additions to the contracted sales backlog from new equipment and monitoring contracts, including renewals and amendments to existing contracts, totalled approximately $12.47 million. These additions were offset by approximately $7.69 million in billings and $0.56 million in net contract terminations related to the Eddy brand.

The contracted sales backlog is an operating indicator and should not be interpreted as recognized revenue, deferred revenue or a measure of future financial performance. ELKHART, Ind.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Patrick Industries, Inc. (NASDAQ: PATK) (“Patrick”) and LCI Industries (NYSE: LCII) (“LCI” or “Lippert”) today announced that their shareholders and stockholders, respectively, have approved the proposals necessary to complete the companies’ previously announced all-stock merger.

“Today marks a significant milestone toward bringing Patrick and Lippert together, and we are grateful for the tremendous support from each company’s shareholders,” said Andy Nemeth, Chief Executive Officer of Patrick. “Our two companies share a deep commitment to our team members, customers and stakeholders, and we believe that together we can deliver more cost-effective, innovative solutions across the Outdoor Enthusiast, Housing and Transportation markets.”

“We appreciate the overwhelming support shown at both meetings today, and we are deeply grateful to the team members who work hard every day in service of our customers,” said Johnny Sirpilla, Interim Chief Executive Officer of Lippert. “For decades, Lippert has earned the trust of customers through innovation, reliability and a culture of service, the same values that have contributed to Patrick’s own growth. We are confident that merging the two companies will extend each company’s legacy in a meaningful way, benefiting team members, shareholders, and the community that we are both proud to call home.”

At the special meeting of Patrick shareholders held today, at least 97% of the votes cast, representing approximately 93% of all outstanding shares, were voted in favor of the four proposals related to the merger. At the special meeting of LCI stockholders held today, approximately 98% of the votes cast, representing approximately 82% of all outstanding shares, were voted in favor of the necessary proposal related to the merger.

The voting results for each special meeting will be reported in Current Reports on Form 8-K to be filed by Patrick and LCI, respectively, with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”). The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027 and remains subject to the receipt of required regulatory approvals and the satisfaction or waiver of other customary closing conditions.
